question: review-1149 KV14: the KV-die landing write path end to end
bench: rtl/test/qwen_kv_die/tb_qkvd_kv_wq.sv (kv_wq_bench.sh), Verilator 5.050 --timing, core 833.333 ps / HBM 1,024 ps
path: posted rows -> ot_qkvd_kv_wq -> 32 x ot_qwen_stream4_cdc_pc (write side) -> HBM-side controller model (hand-off, WR column CTRL_LAT hclk later, write-done) -> 32 x ot_qfd_emb_pcport KVW 2 (SECDED encode, wd two edges after the column) -> HBM array {pc, sector}
checks: every row 4 sectors at pc = {q, t[2:0]}, sec = {layer, g, v, t[13:9], t[6:3]} (computed independently in the bench); the stored 288-b codeword = enc256 of the row bytes and decodes with no error; exactly 4 writes a row, no rewrite; every row retired (rw_v); no fault in the queue / CDC / port
modelled: the per-PC JEDEC scheduler (ot_qwen_ctrl_pc_emb) is a fixed-latency model on the HBM clock (CTRL_LAT 6 / 40): the RTL under test is the write queue, the CDC and the port

mut1.what: write queue: sectors 1 and 2 swap PCs

mut2.what: write queue: sector data from the wrong quarter

mut3.what: write queue: quarter 0 never pushed (row never durable)

mut4.what: pcport KVW 2: KV write check column 0 wrong (ot_qfd_emb_pcport MUT 4)

long.what: 144 rows (36 layers x 4), controller latency 40 hclk

throughput: long run: 144 rows in 9,702 core cycles = 67 cycles a row (rows serialised per queue head), 270 a layer for the 4 rows of a layer: posted, off the token path
rebench: re-benched after the pc_of NBA-index fix (wire array pcq): identical results on all 6 runs
